DZAhv0GvKWh.content: Any psychiatrists or psychiatric mental health nurse practitioners care to help me? Back in 2012, I saw a psychiatrist for workplace discrimination—a severe form of chronic job stress. On Day 1, I was diagnosed with a depressive disorder and prescribed Cymbalta. Part of my employment discrimination involved repetitive stress injuries that were taking too long to heal. By six weeks, I was offered ECT. The doctor was trying to help me. I declined. I explain why in Operation Mental Health: Practical Lessons on Career Burnout and Recovery. The medication left me emotionally numb. Then came the brain zaps, constipation, metallic taste, and profuse sweating. At the time, I was working as a Lung Transplant Coordinator. Eventually, I had to take leave just to detox from the treatment itself. So let me ask again: What percentage of your patients return to work better after FMLA? What percentage return needing accommodations to perform their jobs? Are you helping them access their workplace rights? Are you documenting when workplace conditions may be contributing to poor health outcomes? Because if we are not measuring return-to-work outcomes, how do we know whether we are helping? Black women. Nurses. Employees experiencing chronic job stress. Ask the questions before accepting a treatment plan. You do not need a psychiatric diagnosis to use FMLA. You need a serious health condition. Workplace discrimination, retaliation, and chronic job stress can have profound effects on health, families, finances, and communities. Three months ago, I asked 10 psychiatrists and psychiatric mental health nurse practitioners a simple question about return-to-work outcomes. #fmla #psych #mentalhealth Three months later, I am still waiting for an answer. Take the Work Fatigue Quiz™.

DZKVUpuCfXw.content: Are we celebrating too early? ✋ Two years ago I gave birth to my daughter. I received 20 weeks of paid parental leave. Australia's paid parental leave just increased to 26 weeks. And the government is celebrating. 🎉 But if you've lived through postpartum recovery, you know that 26 weeks is not enough time to heal. Here's what the announcement didn't tell you. Paid parental leave in Australia is paid at the national minimum wage. It's fully taxable. And in the middle of a cost of living crisis, for many families it's financially impossible to survive on. And it's not even 26 weeks for mums, because the pool is shared with your partner, a mother's actual maximum is 22 weeks. Postpartum recovery takes at least 12 months. And can take up to two years after birth. Fewer than half of mothers had fully recovered physically, mentally, and functionally at just 3 to 6 months postpartum. There is a reason postpartum depression is rising. There is a reason birth rates are declining. There is a reason women are leaving the workforce. Giving birth is something you need to recover from. And Australia's paid parental leave system is not built around that reality. Yes, 20 to 26 weeks is progress. But we are nowhere near a milestone worth celebrating. Swipe through to see the full breakdown. → How long did it actually take you to feel like yourself again? Because I have a feeling most of us are still waiting. ↓ #paidparentalleave #postpartumrecovery #australianmums #maternalmentalhealth #maternityleave

DZdAUy0DfxS.content: Recovery doesn't happen by accident. One of the biggest misconceptions about burnout is that rest alone fixes it. While rest is essential, recovery often requires something deeper: systems that reduce the load that created the burnout in the first place. Burnout thrives in chaos, constant urgency, and the belief that everything needs your attention right now. Recovery begins when you create structure that protects your energy instead of constantly spending it. That might look like: Getting thoughts out of your head and onto paper Focusing on a few priorities instead of dozens Planning your time with intention Protecting boundaries around your attention Letting go of what isn't yours to carry Scheduling rest before exhaustion forces it The goal isn't to become more productive. The goal is to become sustainable. At The Burnout Breakdown, we help people understand burnout, recognize the patterns keeping them stuck, and learn about resources and protections, including FMLA, that may provide the time and space needed to recover. Because healing isn't about doing more. You struggle to rest because your mind never gets the message that it's safe to slow down. What many people call "overthinking" is often a nervous system that has been under pressure for too long. Burnout isn't just physical exhaustion. It's cognitive overload. It's carrying so much mental weight that even when you stop working, your brain keeps going. At The Burnout Breakdown, we help people recognize these signs for what they are: indicators that their mind and body may need support, recovery, and time to heal. DZqoYCLEZog.content: FMLA is one of the most misunderstood workplace protections. Many employees wait until they're completely overwhelmed to explore their options because they believe taking leave means they've failed, fallen behind, or put their career at risk. In reality, FMLA was created for the opposite reason. The Family and Medical Leave Act exists to give eligible employees protected time away from work when serious health conditions make it difficult to continue working. That can include physical health conditions, but it can also include mental health conditions when they meet the legal requirements. FMLA is not quitting. It is not giving up. It is not choosing your health over your future. It is recognizing that protecting your health is protecting your future. One of the most common patterns we see in burnout is people pushing through symptoms long after their minds and bodies have started asking for help. They tell themselves they just need to work harder, be stronger, or wait until things calm down. Often, things don't calm down. The exhaustion grows deeper, recovery becomes harder, and burnout begins affecting every area of life. That is why understanding your rights matters. At The Burnout Breakdown, our mission is to help people navigate burnout with accurate information, education, and support. We help workers understand FMLA eligibility, mental health leave options, workplace protections, and the next steps available to them so they can make informed decisions during some of the most difficult periods of their lives. Because asking questions about FMLA is not a sign that you've failed. It may be a sign that you've been carrying too much for too long. Your health matters. Your rights matter. And knowing your options is often the first step toward recovery. #BurnoutBreakdown #FMLA #EmployeeRights #MentalHealthMatters #BurnoutRecovery #BurnoutAwareness #WorkplaceBurnout #MentalHealthLeave #FMLAProtection #WorkplaceWellness #MentalHealthSupport #EmployeeWellbeing #ChronicStress #EmotionalExhaustion #KnowYourRights #MentalWellness #WorkLifeBalance #fyp #viral
